policy_name: India AI Governance Guidelines: Enabling Safe and Trusted AI Innovation
issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India, under the IndiaAI Mission
regulatory_regime: India AI governance (non-statutory; relies on existing laws such as the IT Act 2000 and DPDP Act 2023)

locale_context.regulation: Soft law · principles-based guidelines relying on existing laws
locale_context.culture: Indian innovation-over-restraint, techno-legal approach: AI for inclusive development ('AI for All'), digital public infrastructure, light regulation using existing laws; very large multilingual population.

key_dates.event: Related: IT (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Amendment Rules 2026 on synthetically generated information notified (in force 2026-02-20) - separate binding instrument

covered_entities: government ministries, sectoral regulators and agencies
conditions: proportionate, risk-based application; stronger safeguards suggested for higher-risk uses
objective: Set out a light-touch, innovation-friendly AI governance framework for India built on seven principles ('sutras'), recommendations across six pillars and an action plan, relying primarily on existing laws, voluntary measures and techno-legal approaches rather than a standalone AI law.

related_policies.policy: Information Technology Act, 2000 and IT Rules 2021 (as amended 2026 on synthetically generated information)

conflict_rule: Non-binding; existing statutes (IT Act, DPDP Act, sectoral law) govern; the guidelines recommend targeted amendments rather than a new umbrella AI law.

record_provenance.notes: Official PDF (MeitY/IndiaAI, PIB) could not be fetched; all clauses are paraphrases from law-firm/secondary summaries and have lower confidence. Six pillars reported: Infrastructure, Capacity Building, Policy & Regulation, Risk Mitigation, Accountability, Institutions. Reported institutional proposals: an AI Governance Group (AIGG), a Technology & Policy Expert Committee (TPEC) and a role for the AI Safety Institute - not verified against the text. No evidence found of a revised edition or of the AIGG being formally constituted as of compilation. official_languages: only the English edition was seen in sources; a Hindi edition was not verified.

clauses.original_text: Liability for AI harms should be graded according to the function performed by each actor in the AI value chain, the level of risk and whether due diligence was observed, with each actor responsible for the parts of the lifecycle it controls.
clauses.actor: AI developers, deployers and other value-chain actors

clauses.original_text: Organisations deploying AI should establish accessible (including multilingual) grievance redressal mechanisms through which people can report AI-related harms, process complaints within defined timelines and feed lessons back into risk mitigation.
clauses.requirement: accessible, timely grievance redressal for AI harms

clauses.original_text: A national AI incidents database / reporting system should be developed to record and analyse AI incidents and systemic or technical failures, encouraging reporting without fear of penalty, and kept distinct from end-user grievance mechanisms.
clauses.action: establish and contribute to incident reporting

clauses.section: Key recommendations / practical guidance for industry
clauses.original_text: Industry should publish transparency reports on AI systems, sharing sensitive information confidentially with regulators where appropriate, and adopt voluntary frameworks and techno-legal measures (e.g. content authentication) to manage risks.
clauses.action: publish transparency reports; adopt voluntary measures
clauses.requirement: transparency reporting and voluntary risk-mitigation commitments

clauses.original_text: Higher-risk AI uses should be subject to stronger safeguards, such as human oversight, documented testing, audit trails and the ability to intervene or halt the system.
clauses.requirement: human oversight and testing for higher-risk AI
clauses.condition: where AI use poses higher risk of harm
